v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the Wet meer zekerheid flexwerkers, arguing it does not address the broader labour market problems (two-tier protection and structural staff shortages) without fundamental reform of the permanent contract and related fiscal, social security and pension arrangements, and that the effectiveness of the bandbreedtecontract and the ban on oproepcontracten needs better motivation. The Minister's nader rapport largely rejects the structural critique, pointing to other measures in the arbeidsmarktpakket, while accepting adjustments to the explanatory memorandum, the bandbreedte motivation, simplification of the new articles, the Deeltijdrichtlijn justification and an added Waadi provision.
concerns: The Afdeling argues the proposal fails to tackle fundamental labour market problems and structural staff shortages without reform of the permanent contract and related areas; the government rejects the critique as the package has other measures, but adds explanation to the memorandum.
The Afdeling asks for motivation of the 30% bandwidth and the added value of the bandbreedtecontract; the government motivates the 30% bandwidth and the explanatory memorandum is supplemented.
The Afdeling doubts the effectiveness of the oproepcontract ban given limited supervision by UWV and the Belastingdienst; the government relies on compliance, conversion rules and existing remedies.

The Afdeling asks for justification of the age and part-time exceptions for minors, pupils and students under the Deeltijdrichtlijn and Kaderrichtlijn; the government supplements the objective justification.
The Afdeling finds the new provisions hard to read and asks for simplification; the government simplified and clarified articles 628aa to 628ac and 628a.

36755.s: The bill amends the Omgevingswet's PAS legalisation mandate, renaming it a 'maatwerkaanpak' so that the minister must offer any solution for PAS projects rather than only legalisation. It moves the deadline for the programme's measures to 1 March 2028 and shifts the responsible minister to the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature.
36755.j: The memorandum justifies broadening the options because legalisation alone may not resolve some cases and because a longer deadline is needed for the maatwerkaanpak to succeed.
q: This is therefore a necessary step to make the tailored approach a success.
Het is daarmee een noodzakelijke stap om de maatwerkaanpak tot een succes te maken.
d: adopting a programme of measures to offer a solution for PAS projects
p: Artikel 22.21, eerste en tweede lid (I.B.1, I.B.2)
The minister may offer any solution for PAS projects, not only legalisation, and sets the programme with the broadened discretion; the programme must be carried out by 1 March 2028.

parties: Asks why the nitrogen norm was not set via a ministerial regulation lowering the computational threshold to one mol per hectare, which would have legalised most PAS-melders.

Questions the government on the Raad van State's critical advice, whether it consulted the RvS after amending the memorandum, and what concrete steps support the claim that no nitrogen space can be created.
The Raad van State is not convinced that the proposal actually offers concrete prospects of an adequate solution.
De RvS is er niet van overtuigd dat het voorstel daadwerkelijk concreet uitzicht op een adequate oplossing biedt.
Fears the bill abandons the legal mandate to legalise PAS-projects and gives false hope; doubts it will succeed in obtaining enforcement forbearance given the RvS's core criticism.
These members note that the proposed tailored approach effectively amounts to abandoning the previously statutory mandate to legalise PAS-projects.
Deze leden constateren dat de voorgestelde maatwerkaanpak feitelijk neerkomt op het loslaten van de eerder wettelijk vastgelegde opdracht tot legalisatie van PAS-projecten.
Argues raising the computational threshold is legally risky and could create a new generation of PAS-melders if the threshold is not legally tenable.
Does the government share the view that it is irresponsible to raise this threshold and thereby temporarily legalise PAS-melders if this is not legally risk-free?
Deelt de regering de mening dat het onverantwoord is om deze grens te verhogen en daarmee PAS-melders tijdelijk te legaliseren, als dit juridisch niet zonder risico is?

Supports the bill and urges the government to prevent enforcement against PAS-melders, invoking legitimate expectations and the property right under the ECHR, and asks whether a general pardon is legally possible.
These members call on the government to explicitly declare that enforcement against PAS-melders must always be prevented.
Deze leden roepen de regering op om expliciet te verklaren dat handhaving op PAS-melders altijd moet worden voorkomen.
Notes the bill removes the legalisation obligation and asks about available nitrogen space and the additionality requirement.
These members note that this is not an extension of the deadline in the Environment and Planning Act for legalising PAS-cases, but the removal of the legalisation obligation.

Deze leden constateren dat geen sprake is van het verlengen van de in de Omgevingswet opgenomen deadline voor het legaliseren van PAS-knelgevallen, maar van het schrappen van de legalisatieverplichting.

Says the bill offers no concrete prospects and that without extra source measures the deadline extension merely leaves PAS-melders to their fate; asks about implementing a prior motion and the RvS advice on piekbelasters.
These members deeply regret that the government is evidently placing farmers before a fatal choice.
Deze leden betreuren ten zeerste dat de regering hiermee klaarblijkelijk boeren voor de noodlottige keuze stelt.

Warns that the bill risks disregarding the nature interest, questions how a reasonable balance with natural interests is secured given the court's ruling, and doubts the government's expectation that courts will tolerate non-enforcement.
The nature interest has been insufficiently involved in the decision-making.
Het natuurbelang is onvoldoende betrokken in de besluitvorming.

Argues the bill facilitates the long-term tolerance of unlawful nitrogen-emitting activities, undermines legal certainty and equality, and provokes juridification through enforcement requests by NGOs.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a bill extending the deadline for legalising PAS projects to 1 March 2028, finding that no concrete route to adequate solutions, no source measures, unclear use of the term 'legaliseren', unsubstantiated expectations about enforcement forbearance and missing internet consultation were problems. The minister's nader rapport largely accepted the points: the bill text was changed (legaliseren replaced by maatwerkaanpak / offering a solution), the explanatory memorandum was supplemented, but the minister rejected the call for an overarching programme in the bill and the claim that the bill was urgent to justify skipping internet consultation.
concerns: The Afdeling doubts that the bill offers concrete prospects of an adequate solution for all PAS projects without source measures or a concrete programme of alternative solutions; the minister added explanation on source measures but rejected the demand for an overarching programme of alternatives.
The term 'legaliseren' in the bill text conflicts with the explanatory memorandum's broader meaning, harming legal certainty; the bill text and title were changed accordingly.

The explanatory memorandum's assumption that the new programme increases chances that enforcement forbearance survives judicial review is unsubstantiated; the memorandum was supplemented but the basis was addressed only in part.
The indicative 12-month and phase timeline is doubted as realistic and omits permit procedure time; the minister clarified the term concerns measures and not full implementation.
Internet consultation was omitted without a valid ground; the minister argued urgency, while the Afdeling advised consultation in future cases.

36764.s: The bill implements the EU NIS2 Directive into Dutch law as the Cyberbeveiligingswet, imposing cybersecurity risk-management, governance, and incident-reporting obligations on essential and important entities and designating competent authorities, CSIRTs, and a central contact point. It leaves many details, including the criteria for risk measures, reporting thresholds, and training, to general administrative orders (AMvB) and ministerial regulations, and provides for enforcement by supervisory officials with administrative fines.
36764.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to implement EU directive requirements and to set technical details by general administrative order, while the broad delegations leave substantive rules to the executive.
q: By or under general administrative order, rules are set on the measures referred to in the first paragraph
Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur worden regels gesteld over de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid
d: rules implementing EU implementing and delegated acts and guidelines
designation of essential entities on criteria
cybersecurity risk-management measures and sector-specific requirements
training and certificate requirements for board members
rules on incident notification content and manner
p: Allows a responsible minister to exempt entities active in national security, defence or law enforcement from the risk-management obligations, with exemption excluded for trust services.
Allows ministerial exemption from incident-reporting obligations for entities in national security, defence or law enforcement.

Excludes the Ministry of Defence, intelligence services, prosecution, police and security regions from the Act, and allows an AMvB to exclude further authorities active in national security or law enforcement.

parties: Asks for clarity on the designation process, the role of the coordinating minister, transparency of sectoral rules and the involvement of parliament in oversight of measures.
What safeguards does the government build in to ensure that proportionality is established as objectively as possible?
Welke waarborgen bouwt de regering in om ervoor te zorgen dat evenredigheid zo objectief als mogelijk wordt vastgesteld?

Asks how coordination between sector ministers and the coordinating Minister of Justice and Security works in practice and how conflicts would be resolved, and asks about the regulatory burden advice from ATR.
What is the procedure in case of possible policy conflicts between the sector minister and the Minister of J&V in his role as coordinating minister?
Wat is de procedure bij mogelijke beleidsconflicten tussen de vakminister en de Minister van J&V in zijn rol als coördinerend bewindspersoon?
Asks for clarity on the Raad van State advice about overlapping supervisory bodies, the role of the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and the risk of double supervision with other laws.
These members ask how it is prevented that organisations face dual supervisors and whether the risk of overlapping obligations is sufficiently addressed.
Daarnaast vragen deze leden hoe wordt voorkomen dat organisaties met dubbele toezichthouders te maken krijgen en of het risico van overlappende verplichtingen voldoende wordt ondervangen.
Asks for justification of the stricter-than-minimum choices given the ATR advice, the proportionality of the burden on universities and the funding for the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.
Asks why minimum harmonisation was chosen, requests a list of provisions going beyond the directive, and asks about overlap with zbo supervisory tasks and an impact evaluation after one year.
These members ask whether the government will still address this point specifically and also share this overview.
Deze leden vragen of de regering alsnog specifiek wil ingaan op dit punt en ook om dit overzicht te delen.
Asks about the Raad van State advice on division of tasks with zbo's, the role of ANVS and the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens lacking funding for its supervisory tasks.
Is the government willing to still provide the AP with these funds?
Is de regering bereid de AP alsnog van deze middelen te voorzien?
Asks the government to elaborate on the coordinating role of the Minister of Justice and Security and which zbo's have supervisory and enforcement tasks, as advised by the Raad van State.
Can the government still go into both matters more extensively?
Kan de regering alsnog uitgebreider op beide zaken ingaan?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Cyberbeveiligingswet implementing the NIS2 directive, raising concerns about the coordinating role of the Minister of Justice and Security, overlap with autonomous administrative bodies, supervision of the government sector, personal data processing, exceptions to the Open Government Act, and implementation of Article 32(7). The government's reply (nader rapport) largely accepted these points, amending the bill to clarify exclusions, narrow the sensitive data basis, add safeguards, and implement the proportionality criteria explicitly.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for clarification of the coordinating role of the Minister of Justice and Security and of his involvement in decisions of sector ministers; the government explained the role but kept 'na overleg met' in most cases while using 'in overeenstemming met' where the whole system is affected.
The scope exclusion for public bodies active in national security, defence or law enforcement was too vague, so the bill now lists the excluded bodies explicitly in statute.
The basis for processing special categories of personal data was too broad and lacked specific safeguards; it was limited to necessary tasks with shorter retention periods for CSIRT data.
Implementation of Article 32(7) NIS2 through the general proportionality principle of the Awb was insufficient, so a specific statutory provision was added.

Concerns about overlap with autonomous administrative bodies and independent supervision of the government sector were addressed through explanatory clarifications and reference to the Aanwijzingen inzake de rijksinspecties.
The Open Government Act exception was questioned as a departure from a general law; the government kept it, arguing the statutory exceptions do not give sufficient certainty for confidentiality.
Cooperation and information-sharing purposes, including with intelligence services, were clarified in the bill and explanatory memorandum.

36782.s: The bill amends the Dutch international tax assistance act and the General Tax Act to implement EU Directive 2023/2226 (DAC8), requiring crypto-asset service providers and platform operators to collect and report user and transaction information to the Dutch tax authority, with administrative fines. It also adds registration, reporting obligations, tax-authority access, and enforcement rules for crypto-asset providers and exchanges from 2026.
36782.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations as needed to set detailed verification and reporting rules, and limits judicial review of information requests by pointing to the civil court and the EU deadlines.
q: The bill does not introduce new tax obligations but enables the Tax Administration, by receiving more information, to better check whether existing obligations are complied with on time and correctly.

Het wetsvoorstel voorziet dus niet in de introductie van nieuwe fiscale verplichtingen maar maakt enkel mogelijk dat de Belastingdienst doordat hij meer informatie ontvangt beter kan controleren of de bestaande fiscale verplichtingen van te rapporteren personen tijdig en correct worden nageleefd.
d: due diligence and verification requirements for crypto-asset service providers
verification requirements and reporting rules for crypto-asset providers under the General Tax Act
p: Artikel I, onderdeel J (artikel 6h WIB) and Artikel I, onderdeel R (artikel 10m WIB)
The Minister is given power to automatically exchange taxpayer data with other member states and to remove platform operators from the central register.
Artikel I, onderdeel X (artikel 17 WIB) and Artikel I, onderdeel AA (artikel 30 WIB)
Information-request powers are extended to anti-money-laundering, customs duties and EU sanctions matters.

The tax inspector may impose administrative fines up to the sixth category on providers that fail to report; the memorandum notes only limited judicial review (bezwaar and beroep) of information requests.

parties: Asks how user data is protected, how proportionality is ensured, and what legal remedies users have if their data is wrongly reported, given the international context.
Which legal remedies are available to crypto-asset users if they believe their data has been wrongly reported?
Welke rechtsmiddelen staan gebruikers van cryptoactiva ter beschikking als zij menen dat hun gegevens ten onrechte zijn gerapporteerd?
Asks whether exchange with non-EU countries is legally enforceable, whether the EUR 1,030,000 fine maximum is effective, and about the timing and infringement risks of late implementation.
Is data exchange with non-EU countries legally enforceable?
Is gegevenswisseling met niet-EU-landen juridisch afdwingbaar?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the bill implementing DAC8 (crypto-asset reporting) and raised three points: justification of the high sanction maxima and their proportionality, the absence of a statutory minimum and maximum retention period, and implementation consequences for the Belastingdienst and reporting entities. The government's reply largely explains its choices, adjusts the retention wording and the AWR placement of penalties, and keeps the 31 January deadline and the sixth-category maximum.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for a substantive justification of the sixth-category penalty maxima, including the link to the nature and seriousness of the offence and comparison with other member states; the government explains deterrence and consistency with DAC4 but does not fully add comparative evidence.

The Afdeling doubted that equating the maxima for offences and crimes is proportionate; the government argues proportionality applies case by case and aligns with the Afdeling's earlier advice, and moves the penalty provisions into the AWR's vergrijpboete section.

The Afdeling asked for a statutory minimum and maximum retention period for received data; the government now cites a 12-year period from the selectielijst and commits to explicit statutory retention in a later bill by 31 December 2027.

The Afdeling asked for explanation of implementation consequences for the Belastingdienst (126.1 fte, scarce crypto analysts) and reporting entities, and for weighing the 31 January deadline against the uncertainties; the government keeps the deadline and describes communication measures and a review at end 2026.
Penalty provisions in the AWR are placed in the vergrijpboete section with consistent additional rules, and the reference to the selectielijst is corrected.

36791.s: The bill amends the Dutch rent commission (Huurcommissie) framework: it restructures the commission's chairs into fixed and non-fixed chairs, changes term lengths, removes a complaint procedure against landlords, and lets the commission itself set the service-cost form. It also adjusts procedural deadlines, grounds for challenging members, and the civil code provisions on rent increases for mid-rent housing.
36791.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations and changes mainly by the need for flexibility, efficiency, and a more user-friendly service-cost form.
q: To make these documents mandatory for the procedure before the Huurcommissie, the delegation basis in article 47, sub b, must be extended.
Om deze stukken verplicht te stellen voor de procedure bij de Huurcommissie, dient de delegatiegrondslag in artikel 47, sub b, uitgebreid te worden.
d: ratio of fixed to non-fixed chairs of the commission
Artikel I, S.3 (Uhw art. 47, onderdeel c)
manner in which landlord must give tenant the service-cost overview
Artikel I, S.2 (Uhw art. 47, onderdeel b)
documents tenant must submit with defect-based rent reduction request
service-cost specification form set by the Huurcommissie
p: The commission may extend its decision deadline unilaterally and suspend deadlines when it requests further documents, subject to written notice to the parties.
Procedural rules for challenging (wraking) commission members are tightened, limiting repeat challenges and timing.
Artikel I, T and F (Uhw arts. 4(5), 19aa, 53-55)
The complaint procedure against landlord conduct is abolished, removing a route for tenants to challenge landlord behaviour before the commission.
Artikel I, A.1-A.2 and A.4 (Uhw art. 3a)
A flexible layer of non-fixed chairs without a role in policy-making is introduced, with the composition set by ministerial regulation.
The service-cost form moves from ministerial regulation to the commission itself, with advisory input from the Raad van Advies.
Member terms are shortened to three years with at most two renewals, and the advisory council loses its specific budget and annual accounts advice rights.

parties: Asks how accessibility can be guaranteed for tenants with weak language or digital skills given the mostly written procedure, and whether oral hearings can be preserved.
Are there possibilities to still provide room for hearings where tenants can tell their story orally?
Zijn er mogelijkheden om toch ruimte te kunnen bieden voor zittingen waar huurders mondeling hun verhaal kunnen doen?
Worries that longer deadlines, suspension of deadlines and abolition of the complaint procedure reduce accessibility and protection for vulnerable tenants and independence of the tribunal.
These members stress that the Huurcommissie must remain low-threshold, fast and effective, especially for vulnerable tenants.
Deze leden benadrukken dat de Huurcommissie laagdrempelig, snel en effectief moet blijven functioneren, zeker voor kwetsbare huurders.
Asks about the effects of flexible chairs, the abolition of advisory rights, and whether gemeenten's enforcement capacity may produce unequal protection of tenants.
These members ask the government how it prevents tenant protection from depending on place of residence and municipal capacity (postcode lottery).
Deze leden vragen de regering hoe wordt voorkomen dat de bescherming van huurders afhangt van de woonplaats en gemeentelijke capaciteit (postcodeloterij).
Supports efficiency and the flexible chair pool but asks how quality, consistency of rulings, careful procedure and oversight of the Raad van Advies and flexible chairs will be safeguarded.
These members ask the government to explain how the quality of non-permanent chairs will be guaranteed in practice.
Deze leden verzoeken de regering om nadere toelichting te geven hoe de borging van de kwaliteit van de niet-vaste zittingsvoorzitters in de praktijk zal worden gegarandeerd.
Asks whether the flexible chair pool will include practical and regional housing-market expertise rather than only Hague-based jurists.
These members find that besides legal expertise, knowledge of practice and regional housing-market problems is indispensable.
Deze leden vinden dat naast juridische expertise ook kennis van de praktijk en van regionale woonmarktproblematiek onmisbaar is.
Welcomes strengthening the Huurcommissie but asks how quality, uniformity, independence of members and the balance between written decisions and accessibility are ensured.
These members ask how the quality and uniformity of rulings is ensured when a flexible pool of chairs is deployed.
De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen hoe de kwaliteit en uniformiteit van uitspraken wordt geborgd bij de inzet van een flexibele schil.

Worries procedural changes weaken tenant legal position and accessibility, asks for explicit guarantees of low-threshold access, and questions chair ratio changes made by ministerial regulation without parliamentary involvement.
However, they are concerned that some proposed changes could weaken the legal position and practical accessibility for tenants, especially vulnerable groups.
Echter, zij hebben zorgen dat enkele voorgestelde wijzigingen de rechtspositie en feitelijke toegankelijkheid voor huurders, met name kwetsbare groepen, kunnen verzwakken.
Asks why the administrative structure (merger of zbo and agency) is not being reconsidered now and about the timeframe for assessing the effects of other measures.
These members ask what could be a reason for the government to reconsider the administrative organisation.
Deze leden vragen wat voor de regering wel reden kan zijn om de bestuurlijke inrichting te heroverwegen?
Asks whether the mandatory maximum leges for corporations with four or more losing cases reflects the amendment's intent, which was to allow rather than oblige cost-covering leges.
Does the government agree with these members that this is not in line with the amendment's intent, which states it aims to give the Huurcommissie the possibility to impose cost-covering leges?

Is de regering met deze leden van mening dat dit niet in lijn is met de bedoeling van het amendement, dat stelt dat het amendement ertoe strekt de Huurcommissie «de mogelijkheid te geven» om kostendekkende leges op te leggen, en geen bindende verplichting wenst op te leggen?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division approves of the bill to optimise Huurcommissie procedures but raises concerns about accessibility of the fully written voorzittersuitspraak procedure for vulnerable tenants and asks for the explanatory memorandum to address the long-term governance (hybrid zbo/agency structure, parity, legal unity with municipalities). The government's reply (nader rapport) explains the existing accessibility measures, defends the hybrid structure, parity and the shared legal unity safeguards, defers integration to later, and makes two ambtshalve amendments.
concerns: Accessibility risks of the fully written voorzittersuitspraak procedure for people with limited language or digital skills, which the extended deadlines do not fully address; the government adds explanation of other measures and amends the memorandum.

Long-term reflection on the hybrid organisation (zbo plus agency), the independence concern, and the parity principle; the government rejects the independence concern and defers integration decisions to later.

Preserving legal unity and monitoring overlap between Huurcommissie private-law adjudication and municipal public-law enforcement; the government explains safeguards and monitoring commitments without a legislative change.

36818.s: The bill amends the Dutch international tax assistance act and the global minimum tax act 2024 to implement EU Directive 2025/872 on automatic exchange of global minimum tax information reports among tax authorities, including new definitions, exchange obligations, correction procedures, and a deferred start date of 1 December 2026 for exchanges. The explanatory memorandum argues that bezwaar and beroep are largely excluded for such exchange obligations because a law in the formal sense is not a besluit, leaving civil court interim relief and damages as remedies.
36818.j: The memorandum justifies excluding bezwaar and beroep by stating that a law in the formal sense is not a besluit and that EU exchange deadlines would be obstructed by appeal procedures, with civil court remedies deemed sufficient.
q: A law in the formal sense is not a decision because the legislature in the formal sense is not an administrative organ.
Een wet in formele zin is immers geen besluit omdat de wetgever in formele zin geen bestuursorgaan is.
d: Artikel II B / Wet minimumbelasting 2024 art. 13.1 achtste lid
rules on which report parts go to which authorities
p: The memorandum states that taxpayers cannot bring bezwaar or beroep against the statutory exchange obligations, leaving only indirect or civil court routes for challenge.
The Minister is empowered to automatically share detailed multinational group tax information with foreign authorities on a set schedule, with limited taxpayer recourse.

parties: Asks which countries Netherlands has qualifying agreements with and whether multinationals can choose where to file, and whether the government sees risks there.
Which countries does the Netherlands have such a qualifying agreement with?
Met welke landen heeft Nederland een dergelijke kwalificerende overeenkomst?

Asks the government to justify the purpose of the data exchange, warns against over-reporting, requires safeguards on data protection and retention, and asks for monitoring and evaluation with possible adjustment of rules.
The VVD members attach importance to the data that companies are required to share under this directive being used solely for the intended purpose and adequately protected.
De leden van de VVD-fractie hechten eraan dat gegevens, die ondernemingen verplicht delen onder deze richtlijn uitsluitend worden gebruikt voor het beoogde doel en adequaat worden beschermd.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division had no remarks on the draft bill implementing EU Directive 2025 amending administrative cooperation in tax matters for exchange of minimum-tax data, and advised submitting it to the Tweede Kamer. The government's reply notes the advice is acknowledged and no changes were needed.

36836.s: The bill amends the Temporary Groningen Act and the Mining Act to let the Instituut Mijnbouwschade Groningen pay out assumed mining damage in kind or as reimbursed costs up to a ceiling set by general administrative order, without investigating cause, and to create statutory duties on broader prosperity and sustainability plus an annual State of Groningen report. It also moves the State Supervision of Mines to a collegiate board with an advisory committee and extends several ministerial and regulatory powers.
36836.j: The memorandum justifies the discretion to settle assumed damage without cause investigation as a way to make compensation milder, easier and more humane, consistent with the enquiry's recommendations.
d: maximum amount for assumed-damage handling without cause investigation
I.B (art. 2, 3d lid onderdeel c), I.C (art. 3, 10e lid)
data sharing and processing of personal and health data between designated parties
Instituut may attach conditions to damage handling procedure
further rules on compensation for damage from safety-norm decision
composition, appointment, dismissal and tasks of the advisory committee on board members
p: The Instituut may settle assumed damage without investigating the cause, departing from civil code rules on cause and form of compensation, subject to a ceiling and use of funds for actual repair.
Sunset-type provision art. 20 is removed, making the temporary act's regime open-ended, while an annual State of Groningen report is added as monitoring.
Budget reservations for the reinforcement operation are made for as long as needed, reducing annual parliamentary control over those funds.

The State Supervision of Mines is converted from single inspector-general to a collegiate board, with appointment and assessment handled by the minister and an advisory committee rather than an independent supervisory body.

parties: Asks how the zorgplichten avoid creating expectations that cannot be met, whether the State of Groningen reporting is independent, and whether budget rights of parliament are respected.
Can the government explain why the chosen wording does not lead to limitations of the budget right.
Kan de regering uiteenzetten waarom de gekozen formulering niet leidt tot beperkingen van het budgetrecht.
Has no questions or comments on the Tijdelijke wet Groningen amendment.
These members have no questions or comments on this for now.
Deze leden hebben hier voor nu geen vragen of opmerkingen over.
Argues the zorgplicht has no norm or interim targets, so third parties cannot hold government to account; asks for binding goals and enforceable guarantees for residents.
These members are concerned that only a zorgplicht without a norm is chosen, and they therefore believe concrete goals must be attached to it.

Het baart de leden van de GroenLinks-PvdA-fractie zorgen dat er enkel wordt gekozen voor een zorgplicht zonder norm en deze leden zijn dan ook van mening dat er concrete doelen aan verbonden moeten worden.
Asks how the expected decline in quakes is tested over time, what thresholds would trigger revision, and how spending adequacy is assessed and monitored.
They ask the government to explain how and how often it is assessed whether the original expectations about declining quakes and their visible consequences are still realistic.

Deze leden vragen de regering uit te leggen op welke wijze en met welke frequentie wordt beoordeeld of de oorspronkelijke verwachtingen over het afnemen van bevingen en de zichtbare gevolgen daarvan nog realistisch zijn.
Warns that the new damage route with a 60,000 euro threshold and final release may disadvantage some residents and lock them out of future compensation; asks how legal protection is secured.
These members consider it unacceptable that residents must give final release for damage compensation or damage repair.
Deze leden achten het onaanvaardbaar dat bewoners finale kwijting moeten geven voor schadevergoeding of schadeherstel.
Asks what residents can enforce under the zorgplicht, whether only parliament can hold government to it, and whether a result obligation was considered.
These members ask the government to explain how this zorgplicht will then be enforced.
Deze leden vragen de regering uit te leggen op welke wijze deze zorgplicht dan geëffectueerd zal worden.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on a draft bill amending the Tijdelijke wet Groningen and Mijnbouwwet to implement measures from the government's Nij Begun response to the Groningen enquiry, raising serious objections to the two care duties, the introduction of 'veronderstelde schade' with direct repair up to €60,000 without causation research, the collegiate board of SodM, the multi-year budget obligation and related points, and advising not to submit the bill unless adapted. The government's reply (nader rapport) largely rejects the objections, defends the care duties and direct repair, accepts some drafting changes such as moving the threshold to an AMvB, adds clarifications, and keeps the core measures.
concerns: The care duties (zorgplichten) have an unclear legal meaning and may create expectations that cannot be met; the Afdeling advises dropping them.

Introducing the concept of 'veronderstelde schade' with direct repair up to €60,000 without causation research departs from liability law, causes unequal outcomes, and may raise costs; the Afdeling advises against it.
The explanatory memorandum does not show why SodM needs a collegiate board, and the Afdeling advises against that change, pending the Kaderwet rijksinspecties.
The commission of advice has a dual role that undermines its independence; the Afdeling advises limiting its tasks to advising the board.
The multi-year budget obligation in article 14a conflicts with the annual budget cycle and the parliament's budget right; the Afdeling advises dropping it.
Setting the direct repair threshold by ministerial regulation is too low a level for a core element; it should be regulated by general administrative order.
Data processing of health and personal data needs specific safeguards laid down in law, and the government should clarify sharing rules and protections.
The relation to the Gemeentewet and Provinciewet consultation duties and the meaning of 'overleg' should be explained in the explanatory memorandum.

36863.s: The bill amends the Kieswet to allow voters who need help for reasons other than physical condition to receive assistance when casting their vote in the polling booth, with the assistance provided by a polling station member chosen by the chair or by the voter. It also requires the polling station member to withdraw assistance if the voter cannot unambiguously express their choice, and clarifies the handling of proxy documents in that case; the minister must report on effects within five years.
q: When it becomes apparent to the polling station that a voter needs help for reasons other than their physical condition, the voter is allowed to receive assistance in casting their vote.
Wanneer aan het stembureau blijkt dat een kiezer om andere redenen dan zijn lichamelijke gesteldheid hulp behoeft, wordt het hem toegestaan bijstand te krijgen bij het uitbrengen van zijn stem.

parties: Worries that open-ended third-party assistance could enable mass influence on voters and undermine the secrecy of the vote, and prefers assistance only by neutral polling station staff.

In theory such a scheme opens the door to large-scale influence and erosion of the secrecy of the vote, especially since the notion of 'disability' is not further defined and no medical proof is required.

In theorie opent een dergelijke regeling de deur naar grootschalige beïnvloeding en aantasting van het stemgeheim, temeer daar het begrip «beperking» niet nader is afgebakend en er geen medische bewijslast geldt.
Asks how need for assistance is assessed, whether the secrecy of the vote is effectively breached, and whether the neutrality of polling stations is undermined by familiar helpers.
They ask how it is assessed whether someone actually needs help.
Zij vragen zich af hoe wordt beoordeeld of iemand daadwerkelijk hulp nodig heeft.
Balances the principles of free voting, secrecy and accessibility, accepting some limitation of secrecy for accessibility, and asks whether trained third parties could assist instead.

As the Council of State's advisory division also states, a limitation of the secrecy and possibly the freedom of the vote need not in principle be problematic when it benefits accessibility of the voting process for people with disabilities.

de Afdeling advisering) in haar advies stelt hoeft een inperking van het stemgeheim en mogelijk de stemvrijheid in beginsel niet problematisch te zijn wanneer dit ten gunste komt van de toegankelijkheid van het stemproces voor mensen met een beperking.
Argues that unequal treatment of comparable situations based on physical versus other disabilities is hard to justify and asks for reconsideration and exploration of other assistance options.
They find it difficult to understand that situations comparable in interests and circumstances are nevertheless treated differently based on the criterion of physical disability.
Zij vinden het moeilijk te begrijpen dat situaties die wat betreft belangen en omstandigheden vergelijkbaar zijn toch verschillend worden behandeld op basis van het criterium fysieke beperking.
Asks about the risk of unequal treatment under the Grondwet and IVBPR, clear criteria for staff assessing 'unambiguous' wishes, and evaluation data quality.

These members ask the government what concrete, verifiable criteria polling station members are given to determine whether a voter can express their wish 'unambiguously' and how such assessments are prevented from leading to arbitrariness or divergent practices.

Deze leden vragen de regering welke concrete, toetsbare criteria stembureauleden aangereikt krijgen om vast te stellen of een kiezer zijn wil «ondubbelzinnig» kan uiten en hoe wordt voorkomen dat deze beoordeling leidt tot willekeur of uiteenlopende uitvoeringspraktijken.
Questions why accessibility outweighs voting freedom and secrecy, the risk that all voters can claim help, and whether the rollout should await evaluation of earlier election problems.
Why is more weight given to accessibility and less to other safeguards and fundamental rights such as freedom of the vote and infringement of the secrecy of the vote?
Waarom wordt er een zwaarder gewicht gehangen aan toegankelijkheid en minder gewicht aan andere waarborgen en fundamentele rechten, zoals stemvrijheid en inbreuk op het stemgeheim?
Recognises the dilemma between accessibility for people with disabilities and the constitutional secrecy of the vote, and asks for monitoring and an evaluation involving the target group.
These members recognise the dilemma between improved access to exercising the right to vote for people with disabilities and the constitutional secrecy of the vote.
Deze leden herkennen het dilemma tussen verbeterde toegang tot het uitoefenen van het stemrecht voor mensen met een beperking en het grondwettelijke stemgeheim.
Has no specific questions at this stage and will follow answers from other parties.
These members currently have no specific questions and will follow with interest the government's answers to the questions of the other parties.
Deze leden hebben op dit moment geen specifieke vragen en zullen de beantwoording van vragen van de andere fracties met interesse volgen.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised on a bill allowing voters who need help in the voting booth to receive assistance, mainly criticising the unjustified distinction between voters with physical disabilities and other voters, the insufficient analysis of third-party assistance, a redundant training provision, and the lack of data collection for evaluation. The government's reply accepted the training point and the evaluation/data points, but maintained the two-regime distinction for voters with physical disabilities, citing the UN Disability Convention.
concerns: The distinction between voters with physical disabilities and all other voters lacks sufficient objective justification under the equality principle; the government maintained it on UN Disability Convention grounds and added explanation to the memorie van toelichting.
The explanatory memorandum must further justify why assistance by a trained polling officer is preferred over a third party, which the government expanded upon.
The proposed article J 28b on training is redundant given the existing Kieswet basis and should be deleted; the government deleted it.
Data on assistance given at polling stations must be recorded to allow meaningful evaluation; the government added this to the explanation and will amend the proces-verbaal model.

36872.s: The bill amends the Environmental Act, the General Administrative Law Act and the Offshore Wind Energy Act to implement EU renewables directive III, creating acceleration areas for renewable energy, a screening instrument, a contact point, and direct appeal to the Council of State's Administrative Jurisdiction Division. It also lets the Minister and municipalities set fees and lets the government set by general administrative order (AMvB) rules for designating areas and exempting projects from impact assessments.
36872.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies the delegations and exemptions by the EU directive's requirement to accelerate renewable energy deployment and meet climate targets.
q: In the cabinet's view such circumstances exist, because wind and solar photovoltaic are the main renewable energy sources and without this exemption the targets will very likely not be met.

Naar de mening van het kabinet is sprake van zulke omstandigheden, omdat windenergie en fotovoltaïsche zonne-energie de belangrijkste hernieuwbare-energiebronnen zijn en zonder deze vrijstelling doelstellingen zeer waarschijnlijk niet gehaald worden.
d: criteria for designating acceleration areas for renewable energy
role of the Minister as renewable energy contact point, processing personal data
exemption from appropriate assessment for plans or projects under EU acts, and rules on its application
rules on screening of renewable-energy projects and exemptions from impact assessment obligations
designation of renewable-energy projects with shorter decision deadlines
height of fees charged to offshore wind permit applicants
p: Screening of renewable projects allows authorities to dispense with environmental and appropriate impact assessments in designated acceleration areas, reducing procedural checks on projects.
A general administrative order may exempt plans or projects from the appropriate assessment requirement of the Habitats Directive.[...]
Appeals against renewable-energy permits go directly to the Council of State as the sole instance, removing appeal to the district court and a second instance; judicial review remains available.[...]

parties: Asks whether exempting projects from project MER and nature tests increases legal risk and delay, and whether the Council of State appeals division can handle the added workload.
These members ask how the government prevents exemption from project MERs and nature tests from leading to greater legal risks and thus delay.
Tot slot vragen deze leden hoe regering voorkomt dat vrijstelling van project-MER’s en natuurtoetsen leidt tot grotere juridische risico’s en daarmee tot vertraging.
Welcomes streamlined permitting and shorter appeal procedure but asks how the Council of State's workload impact and the risk of delay will be managed.
The VVD members are satisfied with streamlining the permit procedures and shortening the appeal procedure.
De leden van de VVD-fractie zijn tevreden met het stroomlijnen van de vergunningsprocedures en verkorten van de beroepsprocedure.
Asks how the competent authority will ensure initiators' data is complete and whether the advice of the Commission for Environmental Impact Assessment is followed.
They ask how the competent authority will guarantee that the data provided by initiators is complete.
Zij vragen hoe het bevoegd gezag zal garanderen dat de door initiatiefnemers verstrekte gegevens volledig zijn.

Asks for quantitative justification of the acceleration, since the government says the Dutch system already largely meets RED III deadlines, and questions whether the new screening instrument fits the Omgevingswet's simplification aim.
The JA21 members ask the government to substantiate quantitatively what acceleration this bill actually delivers in the Netherlands.
De leden van de JA21-fractie vragen de regering om kwantitatief te onderbouwen welke versnelling dit wetsvoorstel in Nederland nog daadwerkelijk oplevert.
Argues the bill ignores residents' interests, especially missing distance standards for wind turbines affecting health, and asks how residents will be protected.
They ask the government to acknowledge that wind turbines can literally make residents ill and where those distance standards remain.
Zij vragen de regering te erkennen dat windturbines omwonenden letterlijk ziek kunnen maken en waar die afstandsnormen blijven.
Asks about the status of the nitrogen (ADC) test for energy projects and whether the Habitats Directive allows it at programme level, raising legal-compliance questions.
Is the assumption correct that the Habitats Directive, including its European interpretation, does allow an ADC test at programme level?
Is de veronderstelling juist dat de Habitatrichtlijn, inclusief de Europese interpretatie daarvan, wel ruimte geeft voor een ADC-toets op programmaniveau?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the draft bill amending the Omgevingswet, Algemene wet bestuursrecht and Wet windenergie op zee (implementing parts of REDIII) raises no substantive remarks and may be submitted to the Tweede Kamer. The minister's nader rapport reports only minor drafting changes, clarifying the contact point in article 2.47 and adding coordination provisions with related bills.
concerns: The government clarified in article 2.47(1) Omgevingswet that the Minister of Klimaat en Groene Groei is the contact point, and added coordination provisions linking the bill to related legislation.

36881.s: The bill amends the Dutch housing and planning laws (Algemene wet bestuursrecht, Huisvestingswet 2014, Omgevingswet, Wmo 2015, Woningwet) to strengthen national and municipal steering of housing, with this amendment bill (novelle) correcting parts for legal soundness and feasibility. It removes the absolute ban on urgency status for non-EU foreigners, drops the automatic transfer of permit competence to the minister after a missed deadline, and adjusts the maximum duration of pre-emption rights in the Omgevingswet.
36881.j: The memorandum justifies the removal of the ministerial takeover of permit competence by pointing to its ineffectiveness, lack of ministry capacity, and deviation from interbestuurlijk toezicht principles.
q: This amendment bill provides that this provision lapses for the following reasons.
Deze novelle voorziet erin dat deze bepaling vervalt om de volgende redenen.
d: form for annual overview of urgency applications and permits
p: B (Artikel III, onderdeel FD, Omgevingswet art. 9.4)
Extends the maximum duration of pre-emption rights (voorkeursrecht) held by municipalities, lengthening the period in which owners' property is restricted.

parties: Questions whether the government can guarantee enough social rental housing now that the 30% target is non-binding, and whether the narrowed pre-emption right and regional quotas leave municipalities enough room.
These members note that there is still no guarantee that enough affordable homes will be built.
Deze leden merken op dat er nog steeds geen waarborg is opgenomen die ervoor zorgt dat er genoeg betaalbare woningen worden gebouwd.
Asks the government to justify why the ban on priority for status holders is unconstitutional and whether the limits on appeals and lapse-of-time rules are proportionate.
These members want to ask the government what is missing regarding a 'legitimate aim' and 'reasonable justification'.
Deze leden willen de regering vragen wat ontbreekt inzake «legitiem doel» en «redelijke rechtvaardiging».
Asks how the national government can take over licensing when municipalities stall, and how instruments from the Crisis- en herstelwet remain available, while stressing municipal discretion.
These members ask how the various instruments from the Crisis- and recovery act can still be used under the Versterking regie volkshuisvesting act.
Deze leden vragen op welke wijze de verschillende instrumenten uit de Crisis- en herstelwet wel ingezet kunnen worden onder de wet Versterking regie volkshuisvesting.
Critical of removing municipalities' right to appeal against neighbouring housing plans, calling it a fundamental restriction of municipal legal standing, and asks for proportionality justification.
These members are very critical of this, because it is a fundamental restriction of the legal position of municipalities.
Deze leden zijn hier zeer kritisch op, omdat dit een fundamentele inperking is van de rechtspositie van gemeenten.

Welcomes removal of the discriminatory urgency ban but questions whether the balance under the Omgevingswet has tilted too far towards authorities at the expense of applicants, and asks why the lapse-of-time positive-silence rule is not restored.
does the government not consider the balance in the Omgevingswet to have tipped too far in favour of the administrative authority and thus to the detriment of the applicant
acht de regering de balans in de Omgevingswet niet te veel doorgeslagen in het voordeel van het bestuursorgaan en dus in het nadeel van de aanvrager
Questions how the government protects homeless families' right to urgency when limited by ministerial regulation, and how it meets the 2030 homelessness goal.
Asks technical questions on the frequency of municipal appeals against other municipalities' housing plans and the expected size of the homeless-families urgency category.
The D66 members ask the government to explain how often a municipality has appealed against another municipality's housing decision in recent years.
De leden van de D66-fractie vragen de regering uiteen te zetten hoe vaak een gemeente beroep heeft ingesteld tegen een besluit van een andere gemeente over woningbouw in de afgelopen jaren.
Has no further questions at this stage.
These members have no further questions at this stage.
Deze leden hebben vooralsnog geen verdere vragen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division recommends submitting the novelle without remarks, noting that the original Tweede Kamer process on amendments was rushed and insufficiently considered, which justifies using the novelle instrument. The Minister's reply (nader rapport) confirms the novelle removes the absolute urgency ban for foreigners and the fatal-deadline permit regime, and adjusts the voorkeursrecht rules.
concerns: The absolute ban on urgency status for all foreigners was removed because it conflicted with Article 1 of the Constitution and Article 14 ECHR, as the Afdeling accepted.
The fatal-deadline regime transferring permit power to the Minister was dropped for lack of effectiveness and implementability, which the Afdeling accepted.
The voorkeursrecht provision that could be extended indefinitely risks violating property rights under Article 1 of the First Protocol ECHR, and the novelle adjusts it accordingly.
The Eerste Kamer questioned the implementability of the mandatory urgency category for homeless families with minor children; the government left it to a regulation rather than amending the statute.

36926.s: The bill lets small and medium-sized employers, after 52 weeks of illness, end in-house reintegration and redirect it to work with another employer, with UWV approval or employee consent, and allows replacement of the sick employee. It adds a two-year dismissal ban, a new dismissal ground, and access to the cantonal judge instead of administrative appeal against UWV decisions.
36926.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation to the minister as covering administrative and detailed procedural matters and the exclusion of administrative appeal by avoiding overlapping procedures and speeding up resolution.
q: It is therefore proposed to provide that no objection or appeal is possible against the UWV decision.
Er wordt daarom voorgesteld 30 te bepalen dat tegen de beschikking van UWV geen bezwaar en beroep mogelijk is.
d: procedural rules and data the employer must supply for UWV consent request
p: Allows employers to end in-house reintegration of long-term sick employees with UWV consent, shifting decisions over employee reintegration rights toward employers and the administrative body, subject to employee consent or UWV approval and access to the cantonal judge.
Excludes administrative objection and appeal against UWV decisions on ending the first-track reintegration, leaving only civil court review.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advises the draft bill allowing small and medium employers to end first-track sick-leave reintegration after the first sick year, and says the bill should be reconsidered because it gives limited relief, weakens reintegration chances, and burdens UWV. The government's reply (nader rapport) accepts some points, clarifies others and amends the explanatory memorandum, but keeps the core of the bill.
concerns: The Council doubts the bill meaningfully reduces burdens on small and medium employers, since financial obligations on fixed contracts barely change; the government answers that the aim is flexibility, not cost relief.

The Council argues the bill undermines reintegration chances in the first track and raises WIA inflow, and asks for better motivation; the government acknowledges the risk and points to pilots and a ZonMw programme.
The Council notes significant implementation burdens for UWV on top of existing backlogs; the government says the feasibility test will be refreshed and the start date is 2030.

The Council says the bill sits uneasily with the Wet verbetering poortwachter because agreements between parties can end the first track without UWV review of first-year efforts; the government clarifies safeguards but does not change the design.

The Council asks the explanatory memorandum to address consequences of court rulings after the second sick year, including UWV's handling of dismissal requests and transition payment; the memorandum was supplemented.
The Council asks the explanatory memorandum to address how the planned limitation of transition-payment compensation to small employers affects this bill; the memorandum was supplemented.

The Council asks for a retention period for personal data processed by UWV in the new tests; the government considers statutory retention periods unnecessary and only supplemented the explanatory memorandum.
